# dscal

> Multiplies a double-precision floating-point vector by a constant.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dscal from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/base/dscal';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dscal( N, alpha, x, strideX ) → Float64Array
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | number of indexed elements |
| `alpha` | `number` | in |  |  | scalar |
| `x` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | in |  |  | `x` stride length |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)
- `alpha`: On entry, `DA` specifies the scalar $\alpha$.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: input array

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dscal.ndarray( N, alpha, x, strideX, offsetX ) → Float64Array
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | number of indexed elements |
| `alpha` | `number` | in |  |  | scalar |
| `x` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `x` |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `x` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)
- `alpha`: On entry, `DA` specifies the scalar $\alpha$.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: input array

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dscal()` corresponds to the reference BLAS routine [`DSCAL`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/BLAS/SRC/dscal.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dscal from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/base/dscal';

const N = 3;

// Using the standard interface (scale x by 2):
let x = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, -2.0, 3.0 ] );
let out = dscal( N, 2.0, x, 1 );
console.log( out );
// => <Float64Array>[ 2.0, -4.0, 6.0 ]

// Using the ndarray interface:
x = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, -2.0, 3.0 ] );
out = dscal.ndarray( N, 2.0, x, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
// => <Float64Array>[ 2.0, -4.0, 6.0 ]
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference BLAS 3.12.0 source of `DSCAL`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DSCAL scales a vector by a constant. uses unrolled loops for increment equal to 1.

### Further Details

jack dongarra, linpack, 3/11/78. modified 3/93 to return if incx .le. 0. modified 12/3/93, array(1) declarations changed to array(\*)

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
